before: Before asking someone who is looking for work, “Still haven’t found a job?”, someone who is employed, “How much do you earn?”, a couple without children, “No children yet?”, or someone who is single, “When are you getting married?”, pause and consider.
after: Pause before asking someone who is looking for work, “Still haven’t found a job?” Think twice before asking an employed person how much they earn, a couple without children whether they have children yet, or someone who is single when they are getting married.

before: Behind every answer may be a story the person is not ready to share: worry, loss, disappointment, or simply a personal choice they do not owe anyone an explanation for.
after: Behind every answer may be a story the person is not ready to share: worry, loss, disappointment, or simply a personal choice they do not have to explain.

before: When I asked one of our employees where the assigned task stood, his reply disappointed me deeply.
after: When I asked one of our employees how he was getting on with an assigned task, his reply disappointed me deeply.

before: True, I thought, the world would not fall apart. But what about the trust between us? Will that not collapse too? Would that attitude not harm our working relationship, our mutual respect, and the work we shared?
after: True, I thought, the world would not fall apart. But what about the trust between us? Would that not collapse too? Would that attitude not harm our working relationship, our mutual respect, and our shared work?

before: A delay of a few days was not the real issue. It was his attitude toward a commitment. Responsibility is not only doing the work, but keeping your word, living up to the trust the other person has placed in you, and making sure people can rely on you.
after: A delay of a few days was not the real issue. It was his attitude toward a commitment. Responsibility means not only doing the work but also keeping your word, honoring the trust others place in you, and making sure people can rely on you.

before: Approaching any commitment you have taken on so irresponsibly is not right. Even more regrettable was how that attitude was expressed. To me, such an answer sounds rude, to say the least, and shows too little respect for the other person’s time, effort, and trust.
after: It is wrong to treat a commitment so irresponsibly. Even more troubling was the way he expressed that attitude. To me, such an answer sounds rude, to say the least, and shows too little respect for the other person’s time, effort, and trust.

before: Most disappointing of all, my colleague neither recognized that his words were wrong nor apologized nor completed the task. Because my trust in him had been shaken, I was forced to solve the problem another way.
after: Most disappointing of all, my colleague did not recognize that his words were inappropriate, apologize, or complete the task. Because my trust in him had been shaken, I had to solve the problem another way.

before: Moral: Trust is an organization’s most valuable asset. It takes years to earn and one sentence to lose. The person who stands by his word protects that wealth.
after: Moral: Trust is an organization’s most valuable asset. It can take years to earn and a single sentence to lose. Those who keep their word protect that trust.

before: Javid Bey knew what to do: meet one-on-one and speak in a friendly way. He invited Nadir to the company café on the pretext of having a cup of tea. After a little small talk, he said calmly, “My son, the way you treated Kamal today was wrong. You accused him without understanding the situation, and you did it in front of everyone. Put yourself in his place. He was hoping for our help and was accused instead. I’m sure he hoped we would think the problem through together and find a solution.”
after: Javid Bey knew what to do: speak to Nadir privately and in a friendly way. He invited him to the company café for a cup of tea. After a little small talk, he said calmly, “My son, the way you treated Kamal today was wrong. You accused him without understanding the situation, and you did it in front of everyone. Put yourself in his place. He was hoping for our help and was accused instead. I’m sure he hoped we would think the problem through together and find a solution.”

before: Nadir lowered his head in shame. Javid Bey’s counsel had worked; it was a good lesson for Nadir — he understood he had done wrong.
after: Nadir lowered his head in shame. Javid Bey’s words had taught him a lesson: he understood that he had acted wrongly.

before: Later, whenever Nadir remembered the conversation, he thanked Javid Bey. He was also grateful that no one at the company knew of the conversation between them.
after: Later, whenever Nadir remembered the conversation, he thanked Javid Bey. He was also grateful that their conversation had remained private.

before: Moral: It is a very painful feeling to live knowing you are regarded as unreliable and untrustworthy.
after: Moral: It is painful to live knowing that others regard you as unreliable and untrustworthy.

before: I did not like this phrase “if fate allows” at all.
after: I did not like the phrase “if fate allows” at all.

before: The project team worked tirelessly for months, prepared the documents, and one day, when everything was ready, they sent the materials to the sponsor and began to wait for a response. Days passed, weeks passed. The result — silence.
after: The project team worked tirelessly for months to prepare the documents. When everything was ready, they sent the materials to the sponsor and waited for a response. Days passed, then weeks. Still, there was silence.

before: No one knew. Inquiries to the sponsor brought only evasive, uncertain answers.
after: No one knew. Inquiries to the sponsor brought only vague, evasive answers.

before: When we were schoolchildren, we spent the summer holidays with our family in our garden. My late father wanted to accustom us to hard work, so he left us chores while he went to work. We watered the melons he had planted. We carried drinking water from the well in our neighbor Uncle Aghasalim’s garden, since our own well water was unsuitable.
after: When we were schoolchildren, we spent the summer holidays with our family in our garden. My late father wanted to teach us the value of hard work, so he left us chores to do while he was at work. We watered the melons he had planted. We carried drinking water from the well in our neighbor Uncle Aghasalim’s garden, since the water in our own well was unfit to drink.

before: We learned to turn the soil and clear the weeds, but they were not so easy to clear. One day, Father explained, “You must work deeper. Until you remove the roots, the job isn’t finished.”
after: We learned to turn the soil and pull up weeds, but some were difficult to remove. One day, Father explained, “You must dig deeper. Until you remove the roots, the job isn’t finished.”

before: Moral: Deal with the roots of problems and bad habits. Clearing away only what shows above the surface does not stop it from returning.
after: Moral: Deal with the roots of problems and bad habits. Removing only what is visible above the surface will not keep them from returning.

before: An organization without an action plan is like a ship that knows its destination but has no chart, no chosen route, and no assigned duties for its crew. It may reach port through luck, a skillful captain, or favorable weather. But reaching port would be the result of chance, not of systematic management. Lasting success needs more than fortunate circumstances: it requires careful planning and consistent action.
after: An organization without an action plan is like a ship with a known destination but no chart, no chosen route, and no assigned duties for its crew. It may reach port thanks to luck, a skillful captain, or favorable weather. But that would not be the result of systematic management. Lasting success needs more than fortunate circumstances: it requires careful planning and consistent action.

before: Mr. Aydin was saddened by the state of our school and the hardship we lived in. When he learned that we were all expected to work in the cotton fields after leaving school, his eyes filled with tears.
after: Mr. Aydin was saddened by the state of our school and the hardship we faced. When he learned that we were all expected to work in the cotton fields after leaving school, his eyes filled with tears.

before: How full the world is of wonders and delicate beauty... In every flower, in every whisper of the wind, in the color of the sky, there is a hidden wisdom. This beauty is like a silent trust placed in the human soul. Sadly, however, people sometimes disrupt this harmony with their own hands, burning not only the land in the flames, but also hopes, destinies, and memories.
after: How full the world is of wonders and delicate beauty... In every flower, in every whisper of the wind, in the color of the sky, there is a hidden wisdom. This beauty is like a silent trust placed in the human soul. Sadly, however, people sometimes disrupt this harmony with their own hands, burning not only the land but also hopes, destinies, and memories.

before: War damages not only the land but also the light within us. Every life lost is, in truth, a part of the world falling silent. Yet our purpose in existence is not to destroy, but to protect, create, and sustain life.
after: War damages not only the land but also the light within us. Every life lost is, in truth, a part of the world falling silent. Yet our purpose in life is not to destroy, but to protect, create, and sustain life.

before: Time is a strange wonder... We can neither see it, nor hold it, nor bring it back. It passes silently—in the hands of clocks, in the changing days, in the gray appearing in our hair, in children growing up, in memories receding into the distance...
after: Time is a strange wonder... We can neither see it, nor hold it, nor bring it back. It passes silently—in the movement of clock hands, in the changing days, in the gray appearing in our hair, in children growing up, in memories receding into the distance...

before: In the most delicate and profound layers of human life lies a truth: our relationships are a mirror of our inner selves. The warmth born at the family hearth, the bonds rooted in kinship, the mutual understanding that grows in friendship—each is among life's most precious treasures. The respect and kindness fostered among colleagues are like an unseen light that gives spirit to our daily work.
after: Deep within human life lies a truth: our relationships are a mirror of our inner selves. The warmth born at the family hearth, the bonds rooted in kinship, the mutual understanding that grows in friendship—each is among life's most precious treasures. The respect and kindness shared among colleagues are like an unseen light that brings warmth to our daily work.

before: One of the most precious blessings in a person's life is to receive attention and care. Sometimes even a brief call from a relative, a friend, or an acquaintance, simply to ask how we are, rises like the sun in our hearts. In that moment, we realize that somewhere in this vast world there are people who remember us and consider our presence important.
after: One of the most precious blessings in a person's life is to receive attention and care. Sometimes even a brief call from a relative, a friend, or an acquaintance, simply to ask how we are, rises like the sun in our hearts. In that moment, we realize that somewhere in this vast world there are people who remember us and value our presence in their lives.

before: Everyone needs to be loved, remembered, and valued. A sincere greeting, a heartfelt inquiry, or an unexpected call can sometimes be worth more than the most precious gift. For these small gestures help us feel our place in society and our worth in the hearts of those around us.
after: Everyone needs to be loved, remembered, and valued. A sincere greeting, a heartfelt inquiry, or an unexpected call can sometimes be worth more than the most precious gift. For these small gestures give us a sense of belonging and remind us of our place in the hearts of those around us.

before: One day, while praying in the desert, he noticed a fox with disabled legs. The animal could barely drag itself along. The dervish wondered:
after: One day, while praying in the desert, he noticed a fox that could barely use its legs. The animal struggled to drag itself along. The dervish wondered:

before: “Thank you, Mom. I’m so glad you’re here. With you, I forget both my age and everything I have lived through. May you live long.”
after: “Thank you, Mom. I’m so glad you’re here. With you, I forget how old I am and everything I’ve been through. May you have many more years ahead of you.”

before: “A mother is the one who gives life, son. I am always beside you.”
after: “A mother gives you life, son. I’ll always be here for you.”

before: “You don’t wear me out. I’m tired because I no longer have a mother of my own. There’s no lap where I can rest my head. Don’t you wear yourself out, son. Know the worth of what you have.”
after: “You don’t wear me out. I’m tired because I no longer have a mother of my own. I have no mother’s lap to rest my head in. Don’t wear yourself out, son. Cherish what you have.”

before: Moral: A mother’s embrace is the most comfortable refuge in the world. Whoever has a mother always has a place to rest and lay down their burdens. Know the worth of what you have.
after: Moral: A mother’s embrace is the most comforting refuge in the world. Whoever has a mother has a place to rest and lay down their burdens. Cherish what you have.

before: “If only I could see that young man again. I would tell him that the year he lost gave two people a future. I would ask him to forgive what helping me had cost him. You can learn a profession, my son. What matters is never losing your humanity. He did not leave me alone in that street.”
after: “If only I could see that young man again. I would tell him that the year he lost gave two people a future. I would ask him to forgive me for what helping me had cost him. You can learn a profession, my son. What matters is never losing your humanity. He did not leave me alone in that street.”

before: A court was hearing the divorce case of a couple in their eighties. Everyone in the courtroom was saddened that two people who had shared fifty years together now wanted to part.
after: A court was hearing the divorce case of a couple in their eighties. Everyone in the courtroom was saddened that two people who had shared fifty years of marriage now wanted to part.

before: Moral: Agreement among the many does not make something wrong become right. Sometimes people give up their own judgment and convictions just to be accepted. The real test is to preserve independent thought under pressure, rather than simply become like everyone else.
after: Moral: Widespread agreement does not make something wrong right. Sometimes people give up their own judgment and convictions just to be accepted. The real test is to preserve independent thought under pressure, rather than simply become like everyone else.

before: An Eraser in Marriage
after: An Eraser for Marriage

before: Love was so relieved that it never occurred to Love to ask who had offered to help. Upon reaching the shore, the rescuer dropped Love off and continued on.
after: Love was so relieved that asking the rescuer’s name never crossed their mind. Upon reaching the shore, the rescuer dropped Love off and continued on.

before: “Imagine that today is the last day of the world. By this time tomorrow, everything will be over, and there is no way to escape it. How would you spend the time you have left?”
after: “Imagine that the world will end tomorrow. By this time tomorrow, everything will be over, and there is no way to escape it. How would you spend the time you have left?”

before: The lecturer writes every answer on the board. Then, smiling, the lecturer asks:
after: The lecturer writes every answer on the board, then asks with a smile:

before: “So why are you waiting until the last day of the world to do these things?”
after: “So why wait until the world is about to end to do these things?”

before: “The man lifting stones represents how people become accustomed to wrongdoing. The first time someone does wrong, their conscience weighs heavily on them. Unless they feel remorse and change their ways, doing it again becomes easier. A sin left unrepented can open the door to another.”
after: “The man lifting stones represents how people become accustomed to wrongdoing. The first time someone does wrong, their conscience weighs heavily on them. Unless they feel remorse and change their ways, doing it again becomes easier. An unrepented sin can open the door to another.”

before: Moral: Words can hurt or heal. Their worth lies in speaking with sincerity, kindness and a sense of the right moment.
after: Moral: Words can hurt or heal. Their worth depends on the sincerity, kindness, and sense of timing with which they are spoken.
